FY27/28 MALPF Easement Applications Review The Planning Commission met with Katherine Munson, Planning Manager, Worcester County Environmental Programs, to review the following eleven (11) applications to sell an easement to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) in the FY27/28 application cycle: 1) Beauchamp, Map 99, Parcel 6, 2007 New Bridge Road, 55 acres 2) Beauchamp, Map 99, Parcel 85, Stockton Road, 75 acres 3) Carmean, TM 54, Parcel 18, 6083 Snow Hill Road, 144.5 acres 4) Deuberry, TM 48, Parcel 51, Porters Crossing Road, 82.42 acres 5) Glad Mar Farms, Inc., Map 69, Parcel 15 and Map 77, Parcel 6A (3 acres withheld), Whitesburg Road, 129.71 acres 6) Gravenor, Map 63, Parcel 84, 4915 Pennewell Road, 20.306 acres 7) Maddux, Map 91, Parcel 59, New Bridge Road, 144.92 acres (re-application) 8) Sterling, Map 100, Parcel 30, Payne/Johnson Roads; 73.52 acres 9) Wallace/Hargis, Map 72, Parcel 50, 4308 Paw Paw Creek Road, 205.8 acres 10) Watson Powell Land Holdings, Map 56, Parcel 18, Blake Road, 275.74 acres 11) Watson Powell Land Holdings, Map 56, Parcel 83, Blake Road, 163.02 acres Ms. Munson explained as background that the MALPF program is a state program that purchases permanent agricultural easements on farmland across the state. The county works with the program by managing applications, monitoring easements and providing matching funds (general fund). Funding is mainly generated by the real estate transfer tax and the agricultural transfer tax. Certified counties retain more of the agricultural transfer tax to use for easement purchases. She noted that funding is limited due to the state’s diversion of $25 million from Program Open Space annually through 2029 to address other state budget shortfalls. She provided the Planning Commission with a recent newsletter that is sent to participating and interested landowners. Maps were provided to the Planning Commission showing the location of the applicant properties in relation to protected lands, zoning and the draft growth areas. Individual aerial maps of each property were provided. In response to a question, Ms. Munson stated that funding is likely available for purchase of one or possibly two easements on the applicant properties. Mrs. Wimbrow made the motion to endorse all eleven (11) applications presented, as the applications meet all program requirements and are consistent with the comprehensive plan, and recommend approval of all applications to the Worcester County Commissioners. Mrs. Knight seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously (6-0). III. Comprehensive Plan – Review of Public Comment Mrs. Keener was present to answer questions during the review of public comment on the Comprehensive Plan. Mr. Barbierri questioned whether they should wait to make a recommendation for the Comprehensive Plan until after the moratorium on data centers is lifted, so that the plan would be able to address data centers as well. Mrs. Keener stated that the Comprehensive Plan could address this type of industry more generally and that the Page 2 of 3 WORCESTER COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES – August 6, 2026 Comprehensive Plan guides legislation. Mr. Barbierri asked if there was any additional discussion regarding removing Showell from the growth areas. Mrs. Keener noted that this was part of the original discussion of the growth areas and that the growth capacity in the plan is based on Showell. Following the discussion, a motion was made by Mrs. Knight to provide a favorable recommendation of the plan without any additions or amendments to the County Commissioners. Mrs. Ott seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously (6 to 0). IV. Election of Officers Mrs. Wimbrow made a motion to amend the rules and procedures to remove officer term limits. City of College Park Department of Planning & Community Development Staff Report Reviewer: Carlos Nunes Date: September 24, 2026 A. APPEAL INFORMATION Appeal No.: CPV-2026-03 Hearing Date: October 1, 2026 Petitioner: Andrea & Douglas Schuweiler Address: 5202 Palco Pl, College Park, MD 20740 Subdivision: Sunnyside, Lot 12, Block D Neighborhood Association: North College Park Community Association Zoning: RSF-65 Purpose of Request: The applicants request a variance from Section 27-11002(a) of the Prince George's County Zoning Ordinance to permit expansion of the existing driveway and parking area within the front yard of the dwelling to allow the applicants to park their Recreational Vehicle (RV) off-street. The existing driveway is approximately 9 feet wide by 12.7 feet long. The proposed driveway expansion would create an irregular-shaped driveway/parking area extending farther into the front yard. As shown on the proposed site plan, the expanded area is approximately 30 feet along one side, 23 feet along the opposite parallel side, and approximately 9 feet in width. The requested relief is necessary because the proposed driveway/parking area would extend into the area between the front street line and the sides of the dwelling, where Section 27-11002(a) restricts parking spaces, parking areas, and parking surfaces other than a driveway no wider than its associated garage, carport, or other parking structure. 2 The property possesses an unusual corner-lot configuration, is served by a one-way street, and has a constrained turning area due to the geometry of the roadway, driveway apron, and dwelling. These conditions limit the practical ability to provide additional off-street parking in a zoning-compliant location. Request: A variance from §27-11002(a) of the Prince George’s County Zoning Ordinance to permit expansion of the existing driveway/parking area in the front yard between the front street line and the sides of the dwelling. Requirements: 1. Section 27-11002(a) of the Prince George’s County Zoning Ordinance states: “No parking space, parking area, or parking surface other than a driveway no wider than its associate garage, carport, or other parking structure may be built in the front yard of a dwelling…in the area between the front street line and the sides of the dwelling.” Specific Requests: Approval of a variance to permit the expansion of the existing driveway to: 1. Provide an additional functional off-street parking space to allow the applicants to park their RV off-street; 2. Reduce reliance on on-street parking; 3. Improve vehicle maneuverability by allowing vehicles to access the additional parking area without making a difficult turning movement from the one-way street; 4. Provide additional on-site parking where the property's unusual lot and roadway configuration constrain alternative driveway locations; and, 5. Accommodate the practical parking needs associated with vehicles that cannot reasonably be stored within the existing 8.1-foot wide garage. Property Characteristics: 1. The property contains approximately 8,366 square feet and is improved with an existing single-family detached dwelling that was built in 1954 2. The applicants acquired the property in in 2021. 3. The property is located on a corner lot with an unusual configuration. 4. The dwelling is oriented toward the corner rather than directly toward either individual street frontage. 5. The property has an existing driveway providing access from Palco Place. 3 6. The existing driveway is approximately 9 by 12.7 feet wide. 7. The associated garage door is approximately 8.1 feet wide. 8. The applicants have an approximately 8.5-foot-wide recreational vehicle/truck, which is wider than the existing garage opening and therefore cannot reasonably be accommodated within the garage. 9. The vehicle is also substantially taller than the garage opening further limiting the garage as a practical storage option. 10. The driveway apron is oriented perpendicular to the oneway street, while the existing driveway requires a turning movement to access the parking area. 11. The roadway geometry and existing site configuration create a constrained turning radius for vehicles entering and exiting the driveway. 12. An existing gutter and drainage system is located along the left side of the property with water conveyed underground in that area. 13. The property contains established vegetation and other existing site features that further constrain alternative driveway placement. 14. The proposed driveway expansion is shown as an irregular-shaped driveway/parking area. The proposed area measures approximately 30 feet along one side, 23 feet along the opposite parallel side, and approximately 9 feet in width. 15. The proposed driveway expansion extends beyond the footprint of the existing approximately 9-foot-by-12.7foot driveway and into the front-yard area between the front street line and the sides of the dwelling Neighborhood Characteristics: 1. The surrounding neighborhood consists primarily of single-family detached homes within a residential zoning district. 2. Nearby properties contain a variety of driveway and parking configurations. 3. Several nearby properties have driveway areas that extend beyond the dimensions typically associated with their garages. 4. The subject property is unusual because of its corner-lot configuration and the relationship between the dwelling, driveway, street, and adjoining street frontage. 5. Palco Place is a one-way street, limiting the direction from which vehicles may approach the property. 4 6. A portion of the curb adjacent to the property is marked with a yellow curb/no-parking designation, further limiting the amount of curbside area available for vehicle parking or maneuvering. 7. The roadway geometry and restricted parking area reduce the amount of available space for vehicles to safely maneuver near the existing driveway. 8. Additional off-street parking would reduce the property's reliance on available on-street parking. Other Information: 1. Planning Staff conducted a site visit with the applicants on September 3, 2026. 2. Staff measured the existing driveway at approximately 9 feet wide and approximately 12.7 feet long. 3. Staff observed an approximately 8.5-foot-wide RV/truck on the property. 4. The RV/truck is wider and substantially taller than the existing garage opening, limiting the practicality of using the garage to accommodate that vehicle. 5. Staff observed the one-way street configuration and the yellow curb/no-parking area adjacent to the property. 6. Staff observed the existing gutter and drainage infrastructure along the left side of the property, with water conveyed underground. 7. The drainage configuration and existing site improvements make relocation of the driveway to the western side of the property less straightforward. 8. The applicants reported that their truck has been involved in two hit-and-run incidents in recent months. 9. Staff also observed physical evidence of vehicle maneuvering in the vicinity of the existing driveway. 10. Any work within the public right-of-way, including modifications to the driveway apron or curb, shall require separate approval by the City Engineer and all applicable permits. 11. Any proposed driveway expansion shall comply with all applicable City and County engineering, grading, drainage, and stormwater management requirements. Given the unique physical and contextual constraints described above, the following section evaluates the variance request against the County’s established criteria. 5 COLLEGE PARK CRITERIA FOR GRANTING A VARIANCE 1. A specific parcel of land has exceptional narrowness, shallowness, or shape, exceptional topographic conditions, or other extraordinary situations or conditions that would support the request for a variance. The subject property possesses physical characteristics that distinguish it from a typical interior residential lot. The property is a corner lot with an unusual configuration, and the dwelling is oriented toward the corner rather than directly toward either street frontage. The relationship between the dwelling, driveway, driveway apron, and one-way street creates a constrained area for vehicle maneuvering. The existing driveway is approximately 9 feet wide by 12.7 feet long, while the associated garage opening is approximately 8.1 feet wide. The applicants' approximately 8.5-footwide RV/truck is therefore wider than the garage opening and is not reasonably accommodated within the existing garage. The vehicle's height further limits the garage as a practical alternative. The proposed driveway expansion would extend beyond the existing driveway footprint into the front-yard area. The proposed irregular-shaped driveway/parking area is approximately 30 feet along one side, 23 feet along the opposite parallel side, and approximately 9 feet in width. The street configuration is also unusual. Palco Place is a one-way street, and a portion of the curb abutting the property is marked yellow and prohibits parking. These conditions limit the amount of available curbside area and constrain the way vehicles can approach and maneuver into the existing driveway. The property's existing drainage configuration provides an additional physical constraint. An existing gutter and drainage system along the western side of the property conveys water underground, making relocation or expansion of the driveway in that area less straightforward. These conditions, considered together, create an unusual relationship between the property and surrounding public infrastructure that distinguishes the subject property from a typical residential lot. Staff Finding: The property's unusual corner-lot configuration, dwelling orientation, one-way street, restricted curbside area, constrained turning geometry, existing drainage infrastructure, and limited ability to accommodate larger vehicles constitute physical characteristics that distinguish the subject property. Criterion 1 is satisfied. 1. Denial of the variance will result in a peculiar and unusual practical difficulty to, or an exceptional or undue hardship to the owner. 6 Strict application of §27-11002(a) would limit the width of the driveway to the width of the associated garage and would restrict the location of the parking area within the front yard. The existing driveway and street configuration create a practical difficulty because vehicles must enter the property from a one-way street and negotiate a constrained turning radius to reach the existing parking area. The roadway geometry does not provide the same maneuvering flexibility that would generally be available on a conventional residential street. Additionally, the property is located at the corner which also impacts vehicular traffic movements. The yellow-curbed no-parking area further limits the amount of space available immediately adjacent to the property. As a result, vehicles cannot rely on that area for parking or staging while maneuvering into the driveway. The applicants' larger RV/truck further illustrates the practical difficulty. At approximately 8.5 feet wide, the vehicle exceeds the approximately 8.1-foot width of the garage opening. Its height also exceeds the practical clearance of the garage. Accordingly, the garage is not a realistic alternative for accommodating the vehicle. Staff's site visit confirmed that the existing driveway and surrounding roadway geometry create a constrained vehicle maneuvering area. The applicants also reported that their truck has been involved in two hit-and-run incidents in recent months, further demonstrating the applicants' concern regarding the practical limitations and exposure associated with relying on the existing street environment. Alternative placement of additional driveway area along the western side of the dwelling would also have to account for the existing drainage system and underground water conveyance in that area. The variance would allow the applicants to accommodate additional parking on their property while reducing dependence on constrained public street parking. Criterion 2 is satisfied. 2. Such variance is the minimum reasonably necessary to overcome the exceptional physical conditions. The applicants are requesting relief only to the extent necessary to expand the existing driveway and provide an additional off-street parking space. 7 The proposal does not involve a change in use or an expansion of the dwelling. Expanding the existing driveway allows the applicants to utilize the established driveway access and avoid creating a separate driveway approach or substantially altering another portion of the property. Alternative placement would require consideration of the existing drainage infrastructure along the left side of the property and would create additional maneuvering challenges because of the relationship between the street, driveway, and dwelling. The proposed relief should therefore be limited to the specific dimensions and configuration shown on the final approved site plan. The proposal constitutes a residential site improvement intended to accommodate additional off-street parking on an unusually configured corner lot. The additional parking area would remain accessory to the existing single-family dwelling. Granting the variance would also further the general purpose of the County's offstreet parking requirements by allowing an additional vehicle to be accommodated on private property rather than relying exclusively on limited public street parking. The Zoning Ordinance requires that single family residences provide a minimum of 1.5 parking spaces per dwelling unit, which is then rounded to 2 off-street parking spaces per dwelling unit when there is a single dwelling on the lot. The proposal does not introduce commercial activity, alter the residential character of the property, or otherwise change the established use of the site. Any work affecting the public right-of-way, driveway apron, drainage, grading, or other public infrastructure would remain subject to separate City and County review and approval. The proposed expanded driveway is not of character with the neighboring properties. 8 Staff Finding: The proposed driveway expansion is consistent with the existing residential character of the neighborhood and is not expected to substantially impair the intent, purpose, or integrity of applicable planning documents. Approval of the variance is not expected to substantially impair the use or enjoyment of adjacent properties. The proposed improvement would remain associated with the existing singlefamily residential use and would be located on the subject property. The additional off-street parking would provide an opportunity to accommodate a large vehicle on private property rather than relying upon the limited available curbside area. The one-way street and yellow-curb/no-parking area already restrict parking and maneuvering opportunities in the immediate vicinity. Providing additional parking on the subject property may reduce the need for vehicles associated with the residence to occupy available street parking. The proposed improvement would not authorize a change in use, commercial activity, or expansion of the dwelling. Any potential impacts related to drainage, grading, driveway access, or the public right-of-way can be addressed through the applicable permitting and engineering review processes. Staff Finding: The proposed driveway expansion is not expected to substantially impair the use or enjoyment of adjacent properties and may reduce the property's reliance on limited on-street parking.
